fee.notes: Approximate — the visa fee is commonly quoted around AUD 50 and is often collected on arrival. Confirm the current amount and payment method with Nauru immigration when you apply.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival, and you will need a clear page for the visa label and entry stamp.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only for travelers arriving from, or having transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not formally required, but Nauru's hospital handles only basic cases and evacuation means a charter or a scheduled Nauru Airlines flight to Brisbane — cover with medical evacuation is close to essential.

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed return or onward ticket is part of the visa application and is checked again at check-in. Because flights operate only a few times a week, your dates effectively fix the length of your stay.

proofOfFunds.text: Applicants are expected to show they can cover the trip, and a confirmed, paid accommodation booking — in practice the Menen Hotel or one of a few small guesthouses — is normally required before a visa is granted.

declarations.name: Nauru arrival and customs declaration
declarations.submitWindow: Completed on the aircraft or at Nauru International Airport on arrival
declarations.text: A paper arrival card and customs/quarantine declaration are issued on the flight. Declare all food, plant and animal products — quarantine controls on the island are strict.

currencyLimits.text: Large amounts of cash should be declared on arrival; a threshold equivalent to AUD 10,000 is the usual regional standard — confirm with customs, as Nauru is a cash economy and unexplained sums attract questions.

notes: Quarantine rules are strict: fresh food, seeds, plants and animal products are generally prohibited.
Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons require prior authorization and are otherwise banned.
Duty-free allowances for alcohol and tobacco are small and enforced — declare anything above them.

payments.text: Nauru runs on Australian dollars in cash. Card acceptance is close to non-existent outside the main hotel, ATMs are unreliable or absent, and there is no way to withdraw money if you arrive empty-handed — bring all the cash you will need.

safety.text: Violent crime is uncommon and the island is small enough that visitors are quickly known, but petty theft occurs, alcohol-related trouble happens at night, and medical facilities are very limited. Photography near government buildings and the former regional processing center is sensitive.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Nauru travel information

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is drier and less humid. The November-to-February wet season brings heavy downpours, and the island is hot and humid all year.

tips.text: Start the visa process at least a month ahead. Applications are handled by email with Nauru's immigration office, responses can be slow, and there is no visa on arrival to fall back on — travelers are refused boarding without an approved visa.

Nauru Airlines is effectively the only way in, flying a handful of times a week from Brisbane and around the Pacific via Tarawa, Honiara, Majuro and Nadi. A missed flight can mean several extra days on the island.
Bring Australian dollars in cash for the whole trip, including the visa fee if it is collected on arrival. Assume no working ATM and no card payments.
Rooms are scarce — the Menen Hotel and a few guesthouses cover the whole island. Book and pay before applying for the visa, because the confirmation is part of the application.
Do not photograph government buildings, the airport, the port or the former asylum-seeker processing facilities, and ask before photographing people. Cameras have been confiscated for less.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Nauru?
faq.answer: Yes — essentially every nationality, including Australians, New Zealanders, Britons, Americans and EU citizens, must obtain a Nauru visa before arriving. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa website; applications are made by email to Nauru's immigration authorities with your flight and accommodation bookings attached.

faq.question: How do I apply for a Nauru tourist visa?
faq.answer: You request the application form from Nauru's immigration office, then return it with a passport copy, passport photo, confirmed Nauru Airlines flights, a paid hotel booking and a sponsor or itinerary. Allow two to four weeks, and confirm the current fee — commonly quoted at around AUD 50 — and how it must be paid.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Nauru?
faq.answer: Tourist visas are normally issued for up to 30 days, and in practice the flight schedule sets the length of most visits. Extensions are possible through the immigration office on the island but should not be assumed.

faq.question: What currency does Nauru use and can I pay by card?
faq.answer: Nauru uses the Australian dollar and is a cash economy. Card acceptance is rare and ATMs cannot be relied on, so bring enough Australian dollars in cash to cover accommodation, food, transport and any fees.

faq.question: Is Nauru safe for visitors?
faq.answer: Generally, yes. Violent crime against visitors is rare, but the island has limited medical facilities, few emergency services and a serious road-accident risk on the ring road. Take out insurance with medical evacuation coverage and avoid alcohol-fueled situations at night.
